transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-17 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Alan Chen (Harbor Financial - Head of Compliance), Priya Singh (VP IT Ops), Marcus Williams (Procurement)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. Quick agenda — data residency, compliance controls, logging retention, and then we'll talk about deployment options.
[00:18] Alan Chen: Thanks Jordan. To set context, Harbor serves a lot of EU customers and we have some US retail lines. Primary ask — we need to know if data can be guaranteed to stay in-region, and what logs you keep. Also, what controls for audit and encryption.
[00:35] Samira Patel: Great, thanks Alan. High level: Redwood supports Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Hosted can offer region-based deployments but for strict residency and audit we usually recommend Dedicated or Private — Dedicated gives you single-tenant GPU pools and network isolation; Private gives you customer-managed VPC/on-prem.
[00:52] Priya Singh: When you say "Hosted can offer region-based deployments" — is that the same as GDPR data residency? We need EU-only processing and no routing through US for EU requests.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: Right — for hosted we have EU regions and we can pin model endpoints to those regions. However, logs and some control-plane metadata may be in our US control plane unless we do a Private deployment. So for strict legal/regulatory guarantees, Dedicated with EU-only tenancy or Private is safer.
[01:25] Alan Chen: Can you explain what logs you keep? We have strict logging restrictions, we can't have raw PII in logs for more than 30 days and need the ability to redact.
[01:38] Samira Patel: Sure. By default, our runtime captures request metadata (timestamps, model variant, latency), and optional request/response logs for debugging and quality monitoring. We support automatic PII redaction for common PII patterns, and you can disable full request logging in Dedicated/Private. Retention is configurable; on Dedicated you can set shorter retention windows and we can flush logs on schedule.
[01:58] Marcus Williams: Is the redaction automatic or is that something we have to run post-hoc? We need attestations for auditors.
[02:07] Samira Patel: We offer automated redaction for names, emails, SSNs, account numbers via regex and ML-backed detectors. For attestations, we provide audit logs showing redaction actions, and for Dedicated/Private we can set up a workflow to have logs never leave the customer's VPC.
[02:23] Priya Singh: HIPAA — we have a small product line that touches health info. Is Redwood HIPAA-capable?
[02:30] Jordan Lee: We have customers who are covered entities using Dedicated/Private with BAAs; we can discuss BAA for your specific use-case. For Hosted it's trickier unless it's under a dedicated contractual arrangement and isolation.
[02:45] Alan Chen: Encryption — we need customer-managed keys, KMS integration, and proof that keys never leave our control.
[02:53] Samira Patel: For Dedicated and Private, we support BYOK (bring-your-own-key) with integrations to AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and HSM options. Keys stay in your KMS and we only receive temporary tokens for decryption. For Hosted, we can do envelope encryption but BYOK is typically part of Private or enterprise Dedicated agreements.
[03:15] [03:15] Jordan Lee: Quick note — I'll share our security docs and an architecture diagram after this call (see link placeholder).
[03:22] Alan Chen: GDPR data subject requests — if a customer asks to erase their data, how is that handled if some of the data was used in embeddings or cache?
[03:33] Samira Patel: Good question. We have configurable retention + a KV/prefix cache invalidation API. For embeddings, we can treat them as derived artifacts; we have a deletion workflow that removes the vectors and associated metadata and marks evaluation/training sets. For Hosted we maintain logs of deletion requests; for Private you control the data store so erasure is direct.
[03:55] Priya Singh: We also need to know about export controls and e-discovery. Our legal team will want a list of where data is replicated.
[04:05] Jordan Lee: Under Hosted we do cross-region replication only when explicitly enabled; default region operations keep data in-region, but control-plane data is a special case. In Dedicated we can disable cross-region replication and limit to EU. In Private, no replication unless you configure it. We'll provide a replication matrix in the security brief.
[04:30] Marcus Williams: What about personnel access — do support engineers ever access customer logs? Is there RBAC and SSO?
[04:39] Samira Patel: RBAC is supported; we integrate with SAML/SSO. For Redwood staff access, there's a break-glass process with approval and audit trails. For Dedicated/Private, access can be further restricted and routed through your identity provider.
[04:55] Alan Chen: Timeline: We're aiming to pick a vendor by end of Q2 and run a pilot in July. Procurement wants to know pricing and PO/contract flow.
[05:06] Jordan Lee: That timeline is doable. Next steps I propose: 1) we'll send SOC2/ISO docs and a residency + controls PDF, 2) Samira will propose a bench plan to run Hosted vs Dedicated latency/cost/residency tests (EU-only routing), 3) Harbor shares data classes and retention to scope redaction and logging.
[05:29] Priya Singh: One more — do you support customer-managed log sinks? We want logs pushed into our Splunk in EU region.
[05:37] Samira Patel: Yes, we support push to customer log sinks (Splunk/Datadog/S3) and can restrict endpoint destinations to EU endpoints on Dedicated/Private.
[05:49] [06:00] Alan Chen: For compliance artifacts, can you provide SOC2 type II report and pen test summary?
[06:07] Jordan Lee: Absolutely, will share SOC2 type II, ISO27001 cert, and summary of latest penetration tests; we'll redact sensitive vendor details.
[06:18] Marcus Williams: Procurement question — any minimum committed spend for Dedicated?
[06:23] Jordan Lee: Dedicated is typically reserved capacity with monthly commits; we can propose a small pilot commit for initial bench — we'll include pricing options in the follow-up.
[06:33] Alan Chen: Regarding logs retention — we can't retain request/response logs containing PII beyond 30 days. Can you confirm a hard limit and proof?
[06:42] Samira Patel: On Dedicated/Private we can enforce a hard retention policy at 30 days and configure automated purges; we'll include an audit—exportable deletion proof. On Hosted it's configurable but might not be auditable to the same degree.
[06:58] [07:15] Priya Singh: We also want to understand inference latency across EU regions if we run Dedicated vs Hosted.
[07:22] Samira Patel: We'll include a test plan measuring p95/p99 latencies across typical payloads, token counts, and model variants. For EU-only routing, Dedicated should avoid US egress, so latency differences are mostly model-size and GPU type.
[07:39] Alan Chen: Are there any regulatory restrictions where Redwood refuses service or has export constraints?
[07:45] Jordan Lee: We comply with export control laws and reserve rights per contract; specifics are in legal docs. We'll flag anything relevant once we review your regulated data set.
[07:58] Marcus Williams: Good — sounds like next steps are clear.
[08:05] Jordan Lee: Perfect. I'll send the security pack and a short residency matrix after the call. Samira will send the bench plan. Priya and Alan will send data classification and retention. Marcus we'll coordinate procurement terms.
[08:20] Alan Chen: Thanks everyone.
[08:22] Priya Singh: Thanks.
[08:24] Jordan Lee: Thanks, talk soon.
